title: OpenProjectionFields
description: Open-world key/value projection for material that no pinned structured slot fits (organize v3). It exists so that a real finding in a novel report is not lost just because the closed schemas have nowhere to put it. Three hard limits define what this file is NOT. (1) It is NOT a settled-fact surface: nothing here may be presented to a patient or clinician as an established value, and no formal output (patient_summary / timeline / molecular / treatment_lines / labs / comorbidities / longitudinal_observations / missing_items / readiness / case_summary / charts) may cite it or read from it. (2) It is NOT anchorable: 15_ is not an anchor target, so entries carry their own `open_ref` {source_id, page, bbox} back to the raw page image instead of a bucket source_ref. (3) It is NOT a way around the source-shape invariants: a lab entry still needs its unit and its verbatim source text, and a molecular entry still needs its verbatim source text, so an open filing can never be thinner than the closed one it bypassed. Presence of a lab/molecular entry here does not excuse an empty labs.json/molecular.json — the completeness gates key off inventory clinical_class, not off this file.

source_id.description: MUST match a source_id in source_inventory.json. An entry pointing at a source that is not inventoried is an error, not an orphan to tolerate.

doc_kind.description: Same value as the inventory row's doc_kind (a pinned type name, or novel:<slug>).

clinical_class.description: Same enum as source_inventory. Drives the conditional source-shape requirements below.

label.description: The label AS THE SOURCE PRINTS IT (verbatim, not normalized, not translated). Normalization is a separate, additive layer and does not belong in an open projection. Exactly TWO constraints, and neither is a vocabulary: at most 120 characters, and no control characters. A slug whitelist was rejected deliberately — the whole point of the open projection is material no pinned vocabulary anticipated, so forcing the label through a pinned shape would either mangle it or drop the entry. The cap and the control-character ban are containment (a runaway label cannot become a document-structuring payload), never classification.

value.description: The value as read. Any JSON type; strings keep the source's own formatting.

unit.description: Unit exactly as printed. REQUIRED (non-null) when clinical_class = lab: a unitless laboratory number is uninterpretable and has historically been the single most dangerous silent defect.

source_reported_text.description: The verbatim source substring this entry was read from, e.g. "CEA 12.4 ng/mL (参考 0-5)". REQUIRED when clinical_class is lab or molecular. It is what makes the entry checkable against the page without re-running a model, and it keeps the source-reported layer separate from any normalized reading.

reference_range.description: Reference range as printed by THIS report, when present. Never a range imported from elsewhere.

open_ref.description: Self-contained pointer back to the raw page image. Replaces a bucket source_ref because 15_ is not anchorable; it also anchors to the PAGE, not to a markdown line, so the reference survives re-transcription.

bbox.description: [x0, y0, x1, y1] NORMALIZED to 0-1 against the rendered page, origin top-left. Normalized so the reference stays valid at any render DPI.

text_layer_offset.description: Optional [start, end] character offsets into the born-digital text layer, when one exists.

open_verification_status.description: Verification state of THIS OPEN entry. Deliberately NOT named `verification_status`: every structured output (labs / molecular / patient_summary) carries a `verification_status` whose vocabulary is unverified | clinician_verified | disputed, and the two were read as one field by consumers and by reviewers. They answer different questions — that one asks whether a CLINICIAN attested to a fact, this one asks whether a second READ channel agreed on the characters. `unverified` = read once, no independent channel. `settled` = an independent channel agreed (record which in reread_channel); it still does NOT promote the entry to a patient-facing settled fact — this whole file is off that surface. `needs_human_review` = channels disagreed; both readings must be visible to the reviewer.

reread_channel.description: Which independent channel produced the second read. Same independence rule as source_inventory: re-prompting the same model on the same image is a tie-break, not a channel.

allOf.$comment: A lab reading with no unit and no verbatim source text is not a fact, it is a number. Filing it as an open field must not be cheaper than filing it as a lab.
Variant nomenclature (HGVS c./p., VAF) is exactly where transcription slips; the verbatim string is the only way a reviewer can check it without the model.
